mechanism_narrative: A persistent recovery in workplace and transit mobility raises weekday foot traffic into commercial corridors, so RETAIL_REC should be higher over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are both still far below baseline but slightly less negative at t-0w than at t-1w/t-3w
failure_condition: The hypothesis is rejected if RETAIL_REC does not improve relative to the prior four weeks while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain at least 20 points below baseline throughout the next month.

mechanism_narrative: When residential mobility softens from its recent elevated level, people spend fewer hours at home and make more discretionary retail trips, pushing RETAIL_REC upward within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls at least 1 point week-on-week from its local peak
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is elevated versus baseline in all four weeks and eases from 9.9 at t-2w to 8.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC fails to rise within 14 days after a week-on-week drop in RESIDENTIAL of at least 1 point, or if RETAIL_REC falls despite the residential decline.

mechanism_narrative: If transit remains deeply depressed while workplaces stay below baseline, commuting friction suppresses incidental shopping and keeps RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -35 and WORKPLACES stays below -35 for two consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is about -41 to -43 and WORKPLACES is about -36 to -40 in the snapshot
failure_condition: The hypothesis is rejected if RETAIL_REC does not remain below its prior four-week mean while both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay below the stated thresholds for the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A short-lived jump in PARKS mobility precedes a rotation toward outdoor leisure and away from indoor retail, so RETAIL_REC should fall in the following one-week window after a PARKS spike.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 10 points from the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumps from 14.0 at t-1w to 28.3 at t-0w after a prior decline
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not weaken within 7 days after a PARKS increase greater than 10 points, or if RETAIL_REC rises immediately after the PARKS spike.

mechanism_narrative: An improving grocery-and-pharmacy series together with stable transit indicates broader errand activity and neighborhood circulation, which should lift retail-and-recreation mobility over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stops declining and turns up from a local trough
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improves from -8.6 at t-1w to -7.4 at t-0w while TRANSIT is comparatively stable
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC is unchanged or lower two weeks after GROCERY_PHARM turns up, especially if TRANSIT is also stable or improving.

mechanism_narrative: A continued decline in PARKS after a recent spike signals substitution back toward indoor discretionary activities, so RETAIL_REC should be higher over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS drops for two consecutive weeks after exceeding 20
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from 30.9 at t-3w to 14.0 at t-1w before rebounding to 28.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not rise over the subsequent month after a two-week PARKS decline from an elevated level, or if retail falls while PARKS falls.

mechanism_narrative: If workplaces and transit both remain depressed but residential stays elevated, work-from-home and low-commute conditions dominate daily routines and prevent a retail recovery, so RETAIL_REC should stay lower over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are deeply negative while RESIDENTIAL remains positive in every week
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC rises above its last-four-week mean while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stay suppressed and RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A broad easing across transit and workplaces with no further rise in home-based time produces a lagged pickup in discretionary shopping, making RETAIL_REC higher after one month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES each improve by at least 2 points from their recent weekly lows
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both edge upward at t-0w relative to t-1w, while RESIDENTIAL eases slightly
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days after concurrent improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES, or if RESIDENTIAL rises sharply instead of easing.
